thread.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph><bold>Here's a thread to post useful resources! Please comment any below!</bold></paragraph><paragraph/><paragraph>For example, per my earlier comment:</paragraph><paragraph>If anyone is looking for a nicer way to save the notebook to a pdf, check out this <link href="https://colab.research.google.com/github/Mostafa-MR/Convert_ipynb_to_HTML_in_Colab/blob/main/Convert_ipynb_to_HTML_in_Colab.ipynb">open source ipynb -> html converter</link> I found online. Just download your notebook as an ipynb, upload it as directed to the converter, then print to pdf the resulting html webpage. Super quick & easy.</paragraph></document>
thread.document:
Here's a thread to post useful resources! Please comment any below!



For example, per my earlier comment:

If anyone is looking for a nicer way to save the notebook to a pdf, check out this open source ipynb -> html converter I found online. Just download your notebook as an ipynb, upload it as directed to the converter, then print to pdf the resulting html webpage. Super quick & easy.

comments.content: <document version="2.0"><paragraph>I recently came across an interesting blog post that discusses Muon, its relation to other optimizers, and some open research questions related to it: <link href="https://kellerjordan.github.io/posts/muon/">https://kellerjordan.github.io/posts/muon/</link> </paragraph><paragraph>Edit: There's also this post: <link href="https://jeremybernste.in/writing/deriving-muon">https://jeremybernste.in/writing/deriving-muon</link>. It goes in to the intuitions behind how Muon was derived, some parts of which we briefly touched on in class.</paragraph></document>

comments.content: Probability Playground is one of my favorite sites for building and refreshing probability intuition. It features many important probability distributions with explanations and proofs of standard interpretations and special relationships, and interactive visualizations for exploring the effect of distribution parameters. Fun and informative.https://www.acsu.buffalo.edu/~adamcunn/probability/gamma.html
